items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: if you want to hear great arrangements, listen to anything Johnny Mandel wrote

ctx.x: Well I like those words, especially at 9:50 in the morning. Terrific sentiments.

No but if you want to hear great arrangements, listen to anything Johnny Mandel wrote or Robert Farnon who was the daddy of all the arrangers. He’s got some great albums, Schwartz and Dietz songs, made in England, unbelievable orchestrations.
A recent Joe Williams record he did.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: What do you think Johnny Mandel and these great arrangers, they’ve got maybe a better set of chords than you have see?

ctx.x: Well any words of advice for up-and-coming musicians?

Well you know I always tell the kids if you’re going to play an instrument, learn the chords that you’re doing, just the chords. And then when you improvise the melody you can throw the chords in there. You’ve got it mixed up. You know if you play a single note instrument. If you’re a guitar player, learn the bass note and the chord. And that’s what everything is. What do you think Johnny Mandel and these great arrangers, they’ve got maybe a better set of chords than you have see? They’ve got a substitute here.…
Do you have to pay extra for this guitar though?
